version_guard.provenance: All four guarded probes ran against concrete Claude Code 2.1.302 on 2026-10-17; each ended version-guard: verdict=single-version start=2.1.302 end=2.1.302. Arm S observed concurrent hook execution in 12/12 event pairs with relay-first in 6/12; Arm D verified an errored Bash tool result in each of five denied runs and one Stop per run; Arm T killed all eight overrun firings while all four sessions exited 0 with replies, at 5.1 s after Stop-hook start. The dedicated TUI probe observed one Stop per turn at 4.6 s / 3.6 s. Arm P completed both sequential Bash rounds with --allowedTools=Bash and fired one Stop; the allowed-tool TUI arm of probe-stop-toolallowed completed both turns this time (34.0 s / 27.0 s, one Stop each) rather than timing out as it did on the prior pin. A same-session authenticated claude-print stream-json PTY capture used the same pinned binary; its 39-record stdout was byte-identical to the transcript, with no result, CR, or blank records. The sanitized golden representatives carry forward the 2.1.301 attachment coverage (date, remote_session_change, session_context, prompt_snapshot, agent_listing_delta), all still observed live; no thinking block occurred in this capture, so the thinking/split case is retained from historical evidence. Replay bytes and error objects were verified against the production reader and emitter.

notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host real settings and .claude.json were not read or modified. The host credentials file, when present, was copied file-to-file into the sandbox and never printed.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.302 Arm S: project hook sleeping 300 ms and relay hook 0 ms ran concurrently in 12/12 event pairs; the relay started first in 6/12. The result is concurrency, not a contractual source order: claude-print must not depend on order.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: The dedicated probe-tui-second-turn.sh run on 2.1.302 completed two TUI turns: turn 1 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 4.6 s, and turn 2 fired 1 Stop with SECOND-OK rendered in 3.6 s. probe-claude-contracts T2 turn 1 (multi-round tool use, two loaded sources) fired two Stops - one per loaded source. The allowed-tool TUI arm of probe-stop-toolallowed completed both turns this time (34.0 s multi-round, 27.0 s plain reply; one Stop per turn), unlike the prior pin where it timed out inside the driver window; its Arm P print-mode contract passed.
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Arm D on 2.1.302 used a command-specific Bash deny rule and verified an errored Bash tool result in each transcript. All 5 completed denied runs exited 0 and fired exactly one Stop. The historical 2.1.270 extra-Stop hazard did not reproduce. The poller keeps first-payload tolerance for degraded runs.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Arm P on 2.1.302 used --allowedTools=Bash in the isolated probe project. Both sequential Bash rounds completed in order, the final message was DONE, exit was 0, and exactly 1 Stop fired.
notes.cutoff_evidence: The focused 2.1.302 -p run with --max-turns 2 exited 1 and logged zero new Stop firings; the cutoff remains owned by the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop Poller.
notes.hook_timeout_evidence: Arm T on 2.1.302 configured a relay-position hook with timeout 5 s and sleep 30 s: all 8 event firings were killed, all 4 sessions exited 0 with replies rendered, and each Stop hook-to-process completion was 5.1 s. This confirms the per-hook timeout field used by the relay.
